summary: Backend CRUD/auth/AI regression and mobile Expo preview were tested. Core auth, workspace, incident, checklist, evidence, review, library, history, and AI analysis passed; public health routing and UI testability issues remain.

critical.issue: Public preview URL returns the Expo HTML shell (200 text/html), not the backend JSON health response. /api/health is 404, so the health endpoint is not externally verifiable through the configured ingress.

react_native_issues.issue: Interactive controls have no testID attributes, preventing robust automation and violating the required Expo testability contract.

action_items: Expose backend health through the public /api-prefixed ingress (or configure the ingress exception) and verify JSON status externally.
Add stable testID attributes to auth fields/buttons, navigation, drawer links, modal fields, triage actions, checklist items, and theme switch.
Retest the full mobile incident flow after testIDs are added; the current modal action was difficult to target because the product has no stable selectors.
critical_code_review_comments: Frontend API URL uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL while the stated environment contract names EXPO_BACKEND_URL; current preview works only because the public variant is present.
SSO/Google is intentionally a non-functional alert placeholder, as documented, and is not a backend integration.

success_rate.backend: 75% (3/4 pytest tests; health assertion failed due to public routing)
success_rate.frontend: 75% (preview/auth/workspace/modal passed; extended flow was blocked by selector/viewport targeting)

seed_data_creation: Created TEST_ prefixed preview users and incidents during regression tests; no seeded or existing records were modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: AI analysis returned classification, confidence, findings, report draft, and requires_manual_review successfully. Public /health returned HTML; /api/health returned 404. Preview loaded in 390x844 dark mode and email login/workspace/create modal worked.
rca_of_issue: Ingress routes frontend paths without /api to Expo, while FastAPI defines health only at root /health. Therefore the configured public URL's /health is intercepted by the frontend and /api/health has no matching route. The frontend's missing testIDs makes modal and nested workflow automation fragile.
